subject: Re: Exhibit A - Minimum Protection language and operational impact
messages:
From: Hugo Levesque <hugo@clearwave.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@clearwave.io>
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Exhibit A - Minimum protection redline

Priyom — attaching our annotated Exhibit A (single redline). We're generally supportive of the commercial terms but can’t accept the proposed 'Minimum Protection' carveout in its current absolute form. Two points we want the vendor to consider: 1) if Redwood insists on a hard floor tied to monthly token counts it creates a risk for our seasonal cycles, and 2) the proposed true-up waterfall (section 4.b) would apply penalties before the first 90-day stabilization window.

We redlined to propose a phased floor (quarterly smoothing) and an explicit stabilization period. Also flagged a required ops playbook for billing reconciliations so our finance/AP team can automate true-ups. Please review and let us know if Redwood can accept the phased language or offer an offset (credits or temporary tiered pricing) instead of immediate true-up.

Attachments: ClearWave_ExhibitA_Redline_20261206.pdf (PDF, 1 page redline)

Thanks — Hugo
Senior Dir., Procurement
ClearWave Health

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Hugo Levesque <hugo@clearwave.io>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exhibit A - Minimum protection redline

Hugo — thanks for the quick turnaround and the annotated PDF. Appreciate the context on seasonality. I’m looping in Laura (legal) and Ben (sales ops) to confirm internal flexibility. Two immediate asks from our side:

- Can you confirm which months typically drive the lowest usage (Q4 historically for you?) so we can model the smoothing window?
- Would ClearWave accept a 6-month phased floor with a fixed credit buffer for the first two quarters as an operational compromise?

Internally, I propose we avoid an absolute hard floor in the orderform and instead: 1) define a quarterly averaged floor with a cap on downside true-up per quarter (e.g., max 25% of the floor), 2) add a 90-day stabilization grace for new deployments, and 3) include an ops annex (billing reconciler workflow) that both sides sign off on.

I’ve attached a preliminary counter-redline for internal review — RWI_counter_exhibitA_v1.pdf — which converts the absolute floor into a phased smoothing construct and inserts a one-time stabilization credit. Laura / Ben: please weigh in on legal and revenue recognition implications.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exhibit A - Minimum protection redline

Team — quick legal read on Priyom's proposed approach. High-level: acceptable as negotiation stance, but a few must-haves before we send anything to the customer:

1) Define precise math for 'quarterly averaged floor' (12-week rolling average vs calendar quarter) — recommended: calendar quarter with a reconciliation window to avoid constant re-calcs.
2) Limit the "max downside true-up" to a dollar cap tied to the initial order schedule (so revenue recognition doesn't flip unpredictably). Recommend language: 'the aggregate true-up liability per quarter shall not exceed 25% of the committed quarter fee or $100,000, whichever is lower.'
3) Stabilization period: 90 days OK; add a clause that usage credits applied during stabilization are considered deferred revenue for Redwood (ops/finance note).
4) Ops annex: require that both parties sign the annex within 30 days of execution, otherwise the phased floor defaults to a simple floor with a 60-day extended reconciliation. This gives us an enforceable path if they delay.

I redlined the counter (see attachment) and suggested replacement language in sections 3–5. Ben — please confirm whether a $100k cap is workable for the account, or propose an alternate cap tied to the monthly committed value. Karthik — FYI for pricing impact modelling on Dedicated vs Hosted.

I'll be available for a 20-minute call at 10:30 if you want to triage before sending to Hugo.

— Laura
VP, Legal — Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Hugo Levesque <hugo@clearwave.io>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, legalops@clearwave.io
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 17:42:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Exhibit A - Minimum protection language and operational impact

Hugo — appreciate the patience. Attached is Redwood's counter-redline (RWI_counter_exhibitA_v1.pdf) incorporating a phased quarterly floor, a 90-day stabilization credit, and a capped quarterly true-up liability. Highlights:

- Phased quarterly floor (calendar quarter averaging) with one reconciliation per quarter.
- True-up liability capped at 25% of the quarter fee or $100k, whichever is lower.
- Ops annex requirement: both parties must sign within 30 days of the order; otherwise the fallback reconciliation (60-day extension) applies.

We think this preserves the customer's seasonality concerns while giving Redwood predictable economics and an enforceable ops path. If this is acceptable in principle, we can prepare a short amendment (two paragraphs) for signature and a parallel ops annex template for ClearWave's finance team.

Next steps: 1) Confirm the acceptable cap (is $100k OK?) 2) If yes, I'll send a DocuSign for the amendment and the annex link. HubSpot deal updated here: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/9841

Thanks — looking forward to your thoughts.
Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
